title: Detroit Food-as-Medicine Rx Program
description: Prescription program that connects diabetic and hypertensive patients with subsidized fresh produce boxes from local urban farms, delivered to community pick-up points.
ai_usage: AI personalizes meal plans based on patient health data and food preferences.
long_description: Detroit's high rates of diet-related chronic disease demand innovative approaches. This program bridges the gap between clinical care and food access by enabling physicians to prescribe fresh produce, treating food as medicine. Patients receive weekly boxes of locally grown vegetables, reducing barriers to healthy eating and supporting urban agriculture. Success is measured by improved health outcomes—lower A1C and blood pressure—and increased redemption of prescriptions, demonstrating a scalable model for integrating food systems into healthcare.

title: Food Scrap to Energy Pipeline
description: Establish a citywide curbside food scrap collection system that delivers organic waste to an anaerobic digester, producing renewable natural gas and compost for urban farms.
ai_usage: AI optimizes collection routes and monitors digester performance.
long_description: Food waste is a major contributor to landfill methane emissions, a potent greenhouse gas. By diverting food scraps from the trash, St. Louis can reduce its carbon footprint while creating a local source of renewable energy and nutrient-rich compost. This system not only addresses climate resilience but also supports urban agriculture and food security. Success looks like a citywide program that turns a waste problem into a community asset, with reduced emissions, cleaner neighborhoods, and thriving green spaces.

title: Neighborhood Prescription Pharmacies
description: Establish low-cost, community-based pharmacies in food deserts and high-poverty areas, offering generic drugs, medication management, and health coaching in partnership with local health systems.
ai_usage: AI optimizes inventory and adherence reminders.
long_description: In St. Louis, many neighborhoods lack access to affordable medications, forcing residents to travel long distances or go without. This worsens chronic conditions and drives up emergency care costs. Neighborhood Prescription Pharmacies bring low-cost generic drugs and health coaching directly into high-need communities, improving health outcomes and reducing disparities. By partnering with local health systems, these pharmacies offer medication management and adherence support, while AI optimizes inventory and sends personalized reminders. Success means 10 pharmacies serving 50,000 patients annually, with better medication adherence and reduced hospital readmissions.

title: MealShare App
description: Develops a mobile app connecting restaurants, caterers, and event venues with surplus food to local shelters and food pantries in real time, using a dispatch system to coordinate volunteer pickup and delivery within hours.
ai_usage: AI matches donors with receivers based on location, capacity, and food type preferences.
long_description: Every day, tons of edible food from restaurants and caterers ends up in landfills, while one in six St. Louisans faces food insecurity. MealShare bridges this gap by connecting surplus food donors with nearby shelters and pantries in real time. Using AI, the app matches donors and receivers based on location, capacity, and dietary needs, and coordinates volunteer drivers through a dispatch system. Success means redirecting 100,000 meals annually, reducing waste, and feeding those in need, creating a more resilient and equitable food system.

title: Community Food Forest Network
description: Transforms vacant city lots into self-sustaining food forests—layered with edible perennials—managed by neighborhood associations, providing free, foraging-friendly produce and enhancing green space in historically neglected areas.
ai_usage: AI tracks plant health and predicts yields to schedule harvesting and community events.
long_description:
Food deserts in St. Louis leave many neighborhoods without fresh produce, contributing to health disparities. Vacant lots, often seen as blight, can become productive community assets. A Community Food Forest Network transforms these spaces into layered edible ecosystems, providing free, nutritious food while restoring green space and fostering community pride. Managed by neighborhood associations, these forests offer a sustainable, low-maintenance model of urban agriculture that builds resilience and social cohesion.

Success means 10 food forests across the city, each yielding hundreds of pounds of fruit, nuts, and greens annually. Community members forage freely, while AI-driven monitoring optimizes harvest schedules and organizes events. This initiative not only feeds people but also cools neighborhoods, manages stormwater, and creates gathering places, turning neglected areas into vibrant hubs of health and connection.

title: Emergency Food Delivery Drones
description: Pilots a drone delivery service for emergency food supplies in flood-prone and hard-to-reach neighborhoods, ensuring vulnerable residents receive essentials during disasters, with coordination through the city's emergency management agency.
ai_usage: AI routes drones around obstacles and predicts demand spikes during weather events.
long_description: When floodwaters isolate neighborhoods, traditional emergency food delivery can fail, leaving vulnerable residents without essentials. Drones offer a rapid, resilient alternative, bypassing flooded roads and debris. This pilot uses AI to route drones around obstacles and predict demand spikes, ensuring timely aid. Success means cutting response times to under three hours and delivering 2,000 packages annually, a lifeline during disasters and a model for other cities.

title: Food Waste-to-Energy Loop
description: Deploys decentralized anaerobic digesters at key food waste producers (grocers, hospitals, universities) to convert organic waste into biogas for heating and electricity, with digestate used as fertilizer for urban farms.
ai_usage: AI optimizes waste collection schedules and monitors digester performance to maximize energy output.
impact: 20% reduction in food waste disposal costs
long_description: Food waste is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, and in St. Louis, much of it ends up in landfills. This solution turns that waste into a resource. By installing small-scale anaerobic digesters at large waste producers like grocery stores, hospitals, and universities, we can capture biogas to generate heat and electricity, while producing nutrient-rich fertilizer for urban farms. This closed-loop system reduces disposal costs, creates local energy, and supports urban agriculture, making the city more resilient and sustainable. Success looks like a network of digesters humming across the city, turning waste into power and food, and significantly cutting landfill waste.

title: Schoolyard Orchard Initiative
description: Plants fruit and nut orchards on underutilized school grounds across the city, with maintenance and harvest coordinated by student clubs and parent volunteers, producing free healthy snacks for students and surplus for local food pantries.
ai_usage: AI tracks tree health and predicts harvest yields to schedule maintenance and distribution.
long_description:
Schoolyards are often vast expanses of asphalt and mowed grass, contributing to urban heat and providing little value. Meanwhile, many St. Louis students face food insecurity. The Schoolyard Orchard Initiative transforms these underused spaces into productive fruit and nut orchards, creating a hands-on learning environment and a source of fresh, free produce for students and their families. Surplus harvests are donated to local food pantries, addressing food deserts in surrounding neighborhoods.

Led by a coalition of schools, community groups, and the city's sustainability office, the initiative plants and maintains orchards with student clubs and parent volunteers. AI-powered monitoring tracks tree health and predicts yields, ensuring efficient maintenance and timely harvests. Success means every participating school has a thriving orchard, students learn about nutrition and ecology, and thousands of pounds of fresh produce reach those in need annually.

title: Community Root Cellar Network
description: Establishes a network of refurbished basements in vacant buildings as neighborhood-scale root cellars and food storage hubs, managed by local nonprofits, to reduce post-harvest losses for urban farmers and community gardens.
ai_usage: AI monitors temperature and humidity to prevent spoilage and suggests optimal storage times.
long_description: In St. Louis, urban farmers and community gardeners often lose up to 40% of their harvest due to lack of proper storage. The Community Root Cellar Network transforms vacant basements into shared, climate-controlled storage hubs, dramatically reducing food waste and extending the availability of local produce. By leveraging existing infrastructure and modern monitoring technology, this initiative strengthens local food security, supports small-scale growers, and builds community resilience. Success means a network of cellars across the city, each managed by a local nonprofit, with reduced waste, increased food access, and a more robust local food system.

title: Harvest STL Mobile Market
description: A retrofitted city bus converted into a mobile grocery store that rotates through food deserts in North St. Louis, offering fresh produce and pantry staples at subsidized prices, with stops coordinated with community centers and faith-based organizations.
ai_usage: AI optimizes weekly routes and inventory based on real-time demand and neighborhood demographics.
long_description: In St. Louis, food deserts in North City leave thousands without reliable access to fresh, affordable food. The Harvest STL Mobile Market tackles this by bringing a grocery store directly to the neighborhoods, eliminating transportation barriers. A retrofitted bus, stocked with produce and staples, rotates through community hubs, making healthy food a practical choice for families. Success means more than just sales; it's about dignity, convenience, and improved nutrition. By using AI to anticipate demand and optimize routes, the market stays efficient and responsive, ensuring that fresh food reaches those who need it most, turning a simple bus into a lifeline for the community.

title: Detroit Food Equity Dashboard
description: Interactive online platform displaying real-time data on food access, affordability, and nutrition outcomes across neighborhoods, used by policymakers and community organizations for data-driven decisions.
ai_usage: AI aggregates and visualizes data from multiple sources, highlighting food deserts and trends.
long_description:
The Detroit Food Equity Dashboard will transform how the city addresses food insecurity by making data accessible and actionable. Currently, food access data is scattered across agencies, making it hard to see the full picture. By aggregating and visualizing this data in a user-friendly platform, we can identify food deserts, track nutrition outcomes, and evaluate the impact of interventions. This empowers policymakers and community organizations to target resources where they're needed most, ensuring that every Detroiter has access to healthy, affordable food.

Success looks like a platform that is widely adopted by community groups, health systems, and city departments. With over 100 data partners and 50,000 users annually, the dashboard will become a central tool for decision-making. It will enable proactive measures, such as mobile markets in underserved areas and policy changes that address root causes. Ultimately, this dashboard will help Detroit move towards a more equitable and food-secure future.

title: Detroit Food Hub Network
description: Develops regional food hub in the Eastern Market area to aggregate produce from urban farms and local growers for distribution to schools, hospitals, and retailers, creating economies of scale.
ai_usage: AI forecasts regional supply and demand to minimize food waste and maximize profitability.
long_description: Detroit's Eastern Market has long been a hub for local food, but many urban farms and small growers struggle to access institutional buyers like schools and hospitals due to lack of aggregation and distribution capacity. This solution creates a regional food hub that aggregates produce, uses AI to forecast supply and demand, and distributes efficiently, reducing waste and increasing profitability for local farms. Success means more local food in institutions, stronger farm viability, and a resilient local food system.

title: Detroit Food Rescue App
description: App connecting restaurants, grocery stores, and caterers with food rescue organizations and neighbors in need, enabling real-time pickup notifications and volunteer coordination.
ai_usage: AI predicts food surplus and matches donors to nearby recipients efficiently.
long_description: In Detroit, where nearly half of residents live in food deserts, edible food is often wasted while families struggle to access nutritious meals. The Detroit Food Rescue App bridges this gap by connecting local businesses with surplus food to nearby food rescue organizations and neighbors in need. Using AI to predict surplus and match donors with recipients in real-time, the app reduces waste and improves food access efficiently. With 50 partner businesses and 30 tons of food rescued annually, the app not only feeds people but also fosters a culture of sharing and community resilience. Success is measured by increased food recovery, reduced hunger, and stronger local partnerships.

title: Schoolyard Harvest Program
description: Converts unused schoolyards into edible gardens, managed by students and community volunteers, with produce distributed to school cafeterias and local food pantries.
ai_usage: AI schedules planting and harvest times based on local weather and soil sensor data.
long_description:
The Schoolyard Harvest Program tackles food insecurity by transforming underused schoolyards into productive edible gardens. In Detroit, where many neighborhoods lack access to fresh produce, these gardens serve as vibrant community hubs, providing hands-on nutrition education and fostering a sense of ownership among students. The produce is channeled into school cafeterias and local food pantries, directly addressing food deserts and reducing reliance on distant supply chains.

Success hinges on collaboration: schools, community volunteers, and local nonprofits work together to maintain gardens, while AI optimizes planting and harvest schedules based on soil sensors and weather data. With 20 schools and 4,000 pounds of produce annually, the program enhances food security, builds resilience, and creates lasting environmental stewardship.

title: Food Equity Transit Circulator
description: Free shuttle service connecting food deserts to grocery stores, farmers markets, and food banks, operating on a loop with 30-minute frequency during peak hours.
ai_usage: AI optimizes routes in real-time based on ridership data and service disruptions.
long_description: In Detroit, where nearly half of residents lack reliable access to a vehicle and many neighborhoods are designated food deserts, the Food Equity Transit Circulator bridges the gap. It provides free, frequent rides to grocery stores, farmers markets, and food banks, making nutritious food accessible to all. Unlike traditional paratransit, it operates on a fixed loop, ensuring predictability and ease of use. Success is measured not just by ridership numbers, but by improved food security and reduced isolation.

title: Corner Store Refresh Program
description: Grants and design assistance for corner stores in Detroit's food deserts to upgrade storefronts, add fresh produce, and improve inventory management.
ai_usage: AI conducts market analysis to guide store-specific product mixes and manage perishable stock.
impact: 2,000 residents gain fresh food access per store
long_description: Corner stores are lifelines in Detroit's food deserts, yet many struggle to offer fresh produce due to limited space and supply chain challenges. This program provides grants and design assistance to transform these stores into vibrant community hubs, improving access to healthy food and boosting local economic vitality. Success means upgraded storefronts, increased foot traffic, and measurable improvements in residents' food security.

title: Creative District Night Market
description: A recurring evening market in the Grand Center Arts District featuring local artisans, food vendors, and live performances, with shuttle services connecting to nearby neighborhoods, boosting the night economy.
ai_usage: AI uses mobile ticketing data to optimize vendor mix and adjust hours for peak attendance.
long_description: The Creative District Night Market transforms the Grand Center Arts District into a vibrant evening destination, addressing the cultural district's underutilized after-hours potential. By combining local artisans, food vendors, and live performances, it activates public spaces, supports creative entrepreneurs, and attracts diverse audiences. The market leverages AI to analyze mobile ticketing data, optimizing vendor mix and adjusting hours to match peak attendance, ensuring a dynamic and responsive event. Success means increased foot traffic, economic vitality, and community engagement, fostering a thriving night-time economy that benefits residents and visitors alike.

title: Commercial Composting Hub
description: Establish a centralized composting facility to process food waste from restaurants, grocery stores, and schools, turning it into compost for urban farms and parks. Pilot a curbside pickup for small businesses in two districts.
ai_usage: AI optimizes collection routes and predicts waste volumes to reduce costs.
long_description: St. Louis sends thousands of tons of organic waste to landfills each year, where it generates methane, a potent greenhouse gas. A commercial composting hub would capture this resource, turning food scraps from restaurants, grocery stores, and schools into nutrient-rich compost for urban farms and parks. This not only reduces emissions but also supports local food production and green jobs. The hub would be a central facility where organic waste is processed, with AI-optimized collection routes to make pickup efficient and cost-effective. Success means diverting 5,000 tons annually and serving 50 businesses, creating a model for sustainable waste management in the region.

title: Youth-Led Urban Agriculture
description: Transform vacant lots into student-run farms and markets in food deserts, with curriculum support from local universities and businesses selling produce to restaurants.
ai_usage: AI optimizes crop planning and market pricing based on local demand and weather data.
long_description: Youth-led urban agriculture transforms vacant lots into productive farms, addressing food deserts while providing paid work and leadership opportunities for teens. By growing fresh produce where it's scarce, these farms improve community health and economic vitality. AI tools help youth farmers make data-driven decisions on crop selection and pricing, linking them to local restaurants and markets. Success means sustainable sites run by youth with strong community support, increased access to healthy food, and a replicable model for other neighborhoods.

title: Emergency Food Reserve Program
description: Establish a strategic reserve of shelf-stable food and essentials in community centers for use during disasters or economic shocks, with volunteer packing.
ai_usage: AI monitors supply levels and triggers restocking orders as needed.
long_description: In St. Louis, where food deserts and economic shocks can leave families without meals for days, an Emergency Food Reserve Program provides a critical safety net. By stockpiling shelf-stable food and essentials in community centers, the city can respond within 48 hours to disasters or sudden job losses, preventing hunger and reducing strain on emergency services. Success means every neighborhood has a stocked reserve, volunteers are trained to pack and distribute, and AI alerts trigger automatic restocking, ensuring supplies are always ready. This program builds community resilience and ensures no one goes hungry when crisis hits.

title: Regional Food Hub Logistics
description: Create a regional food hub with cold storage and distribution center to connect small farmers with institutions (hospitals, schools, restaurants) across St. Louis metro.
ai_usage: AI streamlines logistics and forecasts demand to align supply from multiple farms.
long_description:
In St. Louis, many small farmers lack the scale to supply large institutions, while hospitals and schools struggle to source local food. A regional food hub with cold storage and distribution can bridge this gap, aggregating produce from multiple farms to meet institutional demand reliably. This reduces food miles, supports the local economy, and improves food access for residents.

Using AI to forecast demand and optimize logistics ensures efficient operations, reducing waste and costs. Success means more local food on institutional menus, new revenue streams for farmers, and a stronger regional food system. The hub can become a model for other cities, demonstrating how technology can strengthen community food networks.

title: Healthy Corner Store Program
description: Partner with independent corner stores in food deserts to add fresh produce sections, refrigeration units, and point-of-sale signage, with micro-grants.
ai_usage: AI identifies eligible stores via sales data and recommends produce mix based on customer profile.
long_description:
In St. Louis, many neighborhoods lack access to fresh, affordable food, forcing residents to rely on corner stores stocked with processed items. This program transforms these existing retail points into sources of healthy food, bridging the gap without requiring new grocery store construction. By equipping local store owners with the tools and knowledge to stock produce, we support small businesses while improving community health and reducing food deserts.

Success looks like a network of 150 corner stores across the city's food deserts, each with a vibrant produce section. Store owners see increased foot traffic and sales, while residents gain convenient access to fresh fruits and vegetables. The program's use of AI ensures that the produce mix matches local preferences, minimizing waste and maximizing impact. This is a scalable, community-driven solution with measurable outcomes.

title: Food Waste-to-Energy Pilot
description: Install anaerobic digesters at two major grocery chains to convert unsold food waste into biogas and fertilizer, powering nearby community centers.
ai_usage: AI predicts food waste volumes and optimizes collection schedules for efficiency.
long_description: St. Louis sends thousands of tons of food waste to landfills each year, where it generates methane, a potent greenhouse gas. Meanwhile, many community centers struggle with high energy costs. This pilot tackles both issues by installing anaerobic digesters at two major grocery chains to convert unsold food into biogas and fertilizer. The biogas powers nearby community centers, cutting their utility bills and fossil fuel use, while the fertilizer supports local urban farms. Success means diverting 5,000 tons of waste annually, powering 200 homes equivalent, and creating a replicable model for other cities.

title: SNAP Double Dollars Expansion
description: Expand the Double Up Food Bucks program to farmers markets and corner stores, matching SNAP purchases of fresh produce with extra dollars.
ai_usage: AI analyzes purchase data to identify high-impact retailers and target outreach.
long_description: SNAP Double Dollars is a proven strategy to boost healthy food access and local economies. By matching SNAP dollars spent on fresh produce, families can afford more fruits and vegetables, while local farmers and retailers see increased sales. This program directly addresses food insecurity and food deserts in St. Louis, making healthy eating a realistic choice for all residents. Success looks like a thriving network of farmers markets and corner stores where SNAP shoppers feel valued and supported, leading to healthier communities and a more equitable food system.

title: Zero Hunger St. Louis Coalition
description: Create a citywide coalition of food banks, pantries, and meal programs to coordinate food rescue, inventory, and referral services, with shared resource platform.
ai_usage: AI matches surplus food donations with nearby agencies in real-time to reduce waste.
long_description: In St. Louis, food insecurity affects nearly one in five residents, yet tons of edible food go to waste daily. Fragmented efforts among food banks and pantries mean surplus donations often miss those in need. The Zero Hunger St. Louis Coalition solves this by uniting agencies on a shared platform, using AI to match surplus food with nearby organizations in real time, reducing waste and improving access. Success means a coordinated safety net where no edible food is wasted and families find help quickly. The coalition will cut food insecurity by 10% and onboard 80 partners, creating a model for urban food resilience.

title: Neighborhood Food Access Hubs
description: Convert vacant corner stores in food deserts into community-run markets offering fresh produce and pantry staples, with mobile delivery to senior and disabled residents.
ai_usage: AI analyzes foot traffic, sales data, and nutrition guidelines to optimize inventory and suggest healthy swaps.
long_description: In St. Louis, many neighborhoods lack access to fresh, affordable food, forcing residents to rely on convenience stores with limited healthy options. This contributes to higher rates of diet-related diseases and food insecurity. By converting vacant corner stores into community-run markets, we can revitalize these spaces and provide a lifeline of fresh produce and pantry staples. These hubs will be more than just stores; they will be community anchors, offering nutrition education and a gathering place. With AI-driven inventory management, these markets can adapt to local preferences and reduce waste, ensuring that healthy choices are also smart business choices. Success means not only increased access to healthy food but also stronger local economies and improved health outcomes for residents.

title: Downtown Pop-Up Marketplace
description: Revitalize underused downtown St. Louis spaces with rotating pop-up shops and food stalls, managed by a non-profit and city partnership.
ai_usage: AI predicts foot traffic patterns and optimizes vendor mix and scheduling to maximize sales.
long_description:
Downtown St. Louis has seen a rise in vacant storefronts and decreased pedestrian activity, diminishing its historic role as the region's commercial heart. A pop-up marketplace offers a low-risk, high-energy way to activate underused spaces, support local entrepreneurs, and draw people back downtown. By rotating vendors and food stalls, the marketplace creates a dynamic destination that changes weekly, encouraging repeat visits and fostering a sense of discovery.

Operated by a non-profit in partnership with the city, the marketplace uses AI to analyze foot traffic and sales data, optimizing vendor mix and scheduling to align with peak visitor times. This data-driven approach maximizes vendor revenue and ensures the marketplace complements existing businesses. Success means vibrant streets, new small businesses graduating to permanent spaces, and a measurable increase in foot traffic and local spending.

title: Heirloom Seed Saving Circuit
description: A citywide network of community gardens and cultural centers hosts seasonal seed-saving workshops and exchanges, preserving African American heirloom varieties and culinary heritage. Local elders lead storytelling sessions tied to seed histories, with seeds distributed through Detroit's existing food justice programs.
ai_usage: AI matches seed varieties to suitable microclimates and connects participants with similar gardening interests via a community app.
long_description: Detroit's deep agricultural roots and African American culinary heritage are at risk as heirloom seed varieties vanish. This circuit revives that living history by pairing community gardens with cultural centers, where elders share stories behind each seed. Through seasonal workshops and exchanges, families gain seeds and skills, while a community app connects gardeners to suitable microclimates and each other. Success means 200 families annually steward 50 varieties, weaving heritage into the city's food justice efforts, and creating a resilient, culturally rich food system.

title: Vacant Lot Food Forests
description: Transform vacant lots into perennial food forests with fruit trees, berry bushes, and nut groves, managed by local nonprofits and volunteer stewards.
ai_usage: AI recommends suitable plant species based on soil quality, microclimate, and community preferences.
long_description: Detroit's vacant lots, a legacy of disinvestment, can become engines of food sovereignty and climate resilience. Food forests mimic natural ecosystems, requiring less maintenance than annual gardens while building soil health, capturing stormwater, and cooling the neighborhood. They provide a reliable source of fresh, culturally appropriate produce for nearby households, addressing food apartheid and creating green jobs. Managed by local nonprofits and volunteer stewards, these perennial food systems foster community ownership and long-term stewardship. Success looks like a patchwork of thriving food forests across the city, each tailored to its soil, microclimate, and community needs, yielding thousands of pounds of food annually and becoming vibrant gathering places.

title: Creative Coding for Social Change
description: A series of weekend coding bootcamps where youth build apps and digital tools addressing local issues like transportation, food access, or public safety, with showcases to city leaders.
ai_usage: AI code generation tools speed up learning, and an AI ideation assistant helps teens brainstorm app features that address community needs.
long_description: Detroit teens face a skills gap and a civic disconnect. This program bridges both by turning coding into a tool for community action. Over several weekends, youth learn to build apps that solve real problems they see—like unreliable bus routes or hard-to-find fresh food. The result: a new generation of tech-savvy, civically engaged residents, and a pipeline of practical digital tools for the city. Success means not just functional prototypes, but teens who see themselves as agents of change, and city leaders who see youth as partners in innovation.

title: Taste of Detroit Food Fest
description: Annual citywide festival celebrating local urban agriculture and food businesses, featuring cooking demos, tastings, farm tours, and a marketplace, with free admission for low-income residents.
ai_usage: AI analyzes attendance and preference data to curate food offerings and logistics.
long_description:
Detroit's food landscape is marked by stark inequities, with many neighborhoods lacking access to fresh, affordable produce. The Taste of Detroit Food Fest addresses this by transforming a single-day festival into a powerful catalyst for the local food economy. It connects urban farmers, food entrepreneurs, and residents, fostering a vibrant community around food while directly supporting the city's growing agricultural movement. By making the festival free for low-income residents, it ensures that those most affected by food insecurity can participate and benefit from the celebration of local food culture.

The festival operates as a collaborative platform: local farmers and food vendors showcase their products, chefs conduct cooking demonstrations using locally sourced ingredients, and attendees enjoy tastings and farm tours. AI plays a crucial role in analyzing attendance and preference data to optimize vendor selection and layout, ensuring a diverse and appealing mix. Success means 20,000 visitors, 200 vendors, and a measurable boost in sales for participating businesses, while also raising awareness about urban agriculture and healthy eating. The ultimate goal is to seed lasting partnerships and inspire year-round support for local food initiatives.

title: Restaurant Leftover Rescue
description: Deploy 10 electric vans to collect surplus prepared food from 100 Detroit restaurants and caterers, delivering it to shelters and food banks, with a certification program for donors.
ai_usage: AI optimizes pick-up routes and donation schedules using real-time food availability data.
long_description: In Detroit, where nearly 40% of residents face food insecurity, restaurants and caterers discard tons of edible food daily while shelters struggle to meet demand. This program bridges that gap with a simple, scalable solution: electric vans collect surplus prepared food and deliver it to those in need. By leveraging AI for dynamic routing and real-time donation matching, the service reduces waste, lowers emissions, and ensures fresh meals reach vulnerable populations. Success means a self-sustaining network of 100 donors, 2,000 meals rescued daily, and a model that can expand citywide and beyond.

title: Pandemic Harvest Response
description: A rapid-response network of urban farmers and gardeners who pivot to produce emergency food supplies for pantries and senior meal programs during crises, with a citywide logistics hub.
ai_usage: AI predicts food shortages and dispatches supplies to at-risk neighborhoods.
long_description: When the pandemic hit, Detroit's food supply chains buckled, leaving many residents without access to fresh produce. Urban farms and community gardens, already a resilient network, became crucial lifelines. This solution formalizes their emergency role, creating a coordinated system that can pivot within hours to meet urgent food needs. By leveraging AI to predict shortages and optimize distribution, we ensure that help reaches the most vulnerable neighborhoods first. Success means no senior goes hungry, pantries stay stocked, and the city's food system becomes more resilient to future shocks.

title: K-12 Food Literacy Program
description: Integrate hands-on food education into Detroit Public Schools: cooking classes, farm visits, and nutrition lessons, using school gardens as outdoor classrooms, with teacher training and parent workshops.
ai_usage: AI adapts lesson plans to student learning levels and tracks dietary behavior changes.
long_description: Detroit's food landscape is marked by limited access to fresh produce, contributing to health disparities. The K-12 Food Literacy Program tackles this by embedding food education into the school day, transforming schoolyards into learning labs. Students gain hands-on experience growing, cooking, and tasting healthy foods, building lifelong skills and preferences. The program also engages families, creating a ripple effect that extends healthy eating habits into homes. Success means students eagerly eat vegetables, teachers integrate food literacy across subjects, and parents feel empowered to make nutritious choices. This is not just about lessons; it's about cultivating a food-secure future for Detroit's youth.

title: Food Waste to Compost Cooperative
description: Create a citywide network of community composting sites that collect food scraps from households and restaurants, turning them into soil for urban farms and gardens, with revenue from compost sales.
ai_usage: AI optimizes collection routes and monitors compost quality using sensor data.
long_description: Food waste is a major contributor to methane emissions, yet Detroit's urban farms need fertile soil. This cooperative tackles both by creating a decentralized composting network. Households and restaurants separate scraps, which are collected and processed at neighborhood sites. The resulting compost enriches community gardens and is sold to local growers, generating revenue to sustain the program. Success means diverting significant waste from landfills, producing valuable soil, and fostering a circular economy that strengthens community resilience.

title: Schoolyard Orchard Program
description: Transform 20 Detroit schoolyards into edible fruit and nut orchards with student-led planting and care, and harvest distribution to families and local food pantries.
ai_usage: AI models optimal tree species and planting schedules based on climate and soil data.
long_description: Detroit's food deserts leave many families without reliable access to fresh, affordable produce. Schoolyards, often underutilized asphalt or grass, can become productive community assets. The Schoolyard Orchard Program transforms 20 schoolyards into edible fruit and nut orchards, engaging students in hands-on learning about agriculture, nutrition, and environmental stewardship. AI optimizes tree selection and planting schedules based on local climate and soil data, ensuring resilience and productivity. Harvests are shared with students' families and local food pantries, directly addressing food insecurity and fostering a culture of health and community pride. Success means not just trees in the ground, but a sustainable model where students, teachers, and neighbors care for the orchards year after year, creating a lasting impact on food access and education.

title: Mobile Grocery on the Go
description: Deploy 5 retired city buses retrofitted as mobile grocery stores, making weekly stops at senior centers, schools, and transit hubs in food deserts across Detroit, accepting SNAP and EBT.
ai_usage: AI plans dynamic routes using ridership and food demand data to maximize reach.
long_description: In Detroit, nearly 20% of residents live in food deserts, where access to fresh, affordable food is a daily struggle. Mobile Grocery on the Go repurposes retired city buses into rolling markets, bringing groceries directly to neighborhoods, senior centers, and schools. These buses accept SNAP and EBT, making healthy food accessible to those who need it most. By leveraging AI to optimize routes based on demand, the service maximizes efficiency and reach. Success means more than just food access—it's about dignity, community health, and reducing the burden of transportation. With 5 buses, we can serve 15,000 residents, making 300 weekly stops, and turn food deserts into food oases.

title: Corner Store Fresh Conversion
description: Partner with 50 corner stores in underserved areas to add fresh produce and healthy staples through low-cost equipment grants, training, and supply chain connections, turning them into neighborhood healthy food hubs.
ai_usage: AI predicts sales trends and waste to optimize produce ordering and reduce spoilage.
long_description: In Detroit, many neighborhoods lack supermarkets, forcing residents to rely on corner stores that stock mostly processed foods. This initiative transforms these stores into sources of fresh produce and healthy staples, addressing food deserts at the neighborhood level. By providing equipment grants, training, and supply chain connections, we empower store owners to become community health hubs. Success means improved food access, increased sales for store owners, and better health outcomes for residents. AI-driven inventory management minimizes waste and ensures consistent supply, making the model sustainable.

title: Detroit Food Co-op Network
description: Launch a network of member-owned grocery co-ops in food deserts across Detroit, starting with neighborhoods like the North End and southwest, using vacant storefronts and offering fresh produce, staples, and community space.
ai_usage: AI analyzes demographic and spending data to pinpoint optimal co-op locations and product mixes.
long_description: Detroit's food deserts leave thousands without access to fresh, affordable groceries, contributing to health disparities and economic stagnation. A network of member-owned co-ops, rooted in community ownership, can transform vacant storefronts into vibrant hubs of food and connection. By leveraging AI to pinpoint demand and optimize product mixes, these co-ops can be financially sustainable while empowering residents. Success means 10 co-ops by 2028, serving 40,000 members, and revitalizing neighborhoods from the North End to southwest Detroit.

title: Motor City Makers Market
description: A network of rotating pop-up markets in vacant lots and underused plazas across Detroit neighborhoods, featuring local artisans, food entrepreneurs, and small-batch manufacturers. Managed by neighborhood associations with support for permits, insurance, and marketing.
ai_usage: AI predicts optimal market locations and dates based on foot traffic, weather, and sales data to maximize attendance.
long_description: Detroit's vacant lots and underused plazas are more than blight—they are opportunities for economic revival. The Motor City Makers Market transforms these spaces into vibrant commercial hubs, connecting local artisans and food entrepreneurs with eager customers. By rotating through neighborhoods, the market spreads foot traffic and spending, supporting small businesses that often lack access to traditional retail. Success means not just sales, but a renewed sense of place and pride, with neighbors gathering to shop, eat, and celebrate local craft.

title: Food Scrap to Energy Loop
description: Partner with large food producers and hospitals to collect organic waste, which is digested anaerobically to produce biogas for heating or electricity, while the digestate becomes fertilizer for urban farms.
ai_usage: AI coordinates waste collection logistics and optimizes biogas production based on feedstock variety.
long_description: St. Louis sends thousands of tons of organic waste to landfills each year, where it decomposes and releases methane, a potent greenhouse gas. By capturing this waste from large food producers and hospitals, we can turn a liability into an asset: producing renewable biogas and nutrient-rich fertilizer. This loop reduces emissions, supports local food systems, and cuts waste disposal costs. Success means a self-sustaining system that diverts 10,000 tons annually, powers 1,000 homes, and enriches urban farms, demonstrating a replicable model for other cities.

title: Food Justice Data Commons
description: Regional open-data platform aggregating food access, insecurity, and supply chain data to inform city policy and community action.
ai_usage: AI integrates and visualizes data to identify emerging food deserts and vulnerable population clusters.
long_description: Food deserts are not static; they shift with grocery store closures, transit changes, and economic shocks. The Food Justice Data Commons would aggregate scattered data from the city, regional food banks, and community organizations into a single, open platform. Using AI to visualize and analyze this data, the platform can identify emerging food deserts and vulnerable populations in real time, enabling proactive policy and community action. Success means that over 100 data sources are integrated and at least 20 community organizations actively use the platform to inform their work, leading to more equitable food access across St. Louis.

title: Farm-to-Neighborhood Truck Program
description: A fleet of refrigerated trucks carrying fresh produce from regional farms directly to neighborhood pop-up markets in food deserts, priced affordably.
ai_usage: AI forecasts market demand and farm surplus to plan route stops and inventory.
long_description:
In St. Louis, many neighborhoods lack access to fresh, affordable produce, forcing residents to rely on convenience stores and fast food. This program bridges the gap by bringing farm-fresh goods directly to these food deserts via refrigerated trucks, creating mobile markets that are both accessible and cost-effective. By leveraging AI to optimize routes and inventory based on demand and surplus, the program reduces waste and ensures a steady supply of nutritious options.

Success looks like a reliable network of pop-up markets that serve thousands of households weekly, with produce priced 40% below retail. This not only improves food security but also supports local farmers and fosters community resilience. The program is designed to be scalable and replicable, with a clear path from pilot to citywide implementation.

title: Emergency Food Voucher System
description: Digitized emergency food vouchers for rapidly deployable food assistance during crises, integrated with local food pantries and mobile markets.
ai_usage: AI predicts crisis impact zones and pre-authorizes voucher distribution to at-risk households.
long_description: When a crisis hits, families already on the edge can be pushed into immediate food insecurity. Traditional emergency food systems rely on physical distribution, which can be slow and inequitable. The Emergency Food Voucher System uses AI to predict impact zones and pre-authorize digital vouchers to at-risk households, enabling rapid, dignified access to food at local pantries and mobile markets. Success means a two-day turnaround from crisis declaration to voucher use, reducing hunger and strain on emergency services. This system also builds a responsive infrastructure that can adapt to future shocks, making the city more resilient.

title: Community Seafood Hub
description: A network of small-scale aquaculture farms in repurposed warehouses, raising fish and aquaponic vegetables, with a distribution hub for local seafood.
ai_usage: AI monitors water quality and feeding schedules to optimize fish health and yield.
long_description: St. Louis households in food deserts often lack access to fresh, affordable protein. A Community Seafood Hub can transform underutilized warehouses into productive aquaponic farms, raising fish and vegetables in a closed-loop system. This provides a local, sustainable protein source while creating green jobs and revitalizing vacant properties. AI-driven monitoring ensures optimal water quality and feeding, reducing labor and increasing yield. Success means a resilient food network that supplies restaurants, grocers, and food pantries, and serves as a model for other cities.

title: Food Waste Digester Network
description: Install community-scale anaerobic digesters to process organic waste from households and businesses into biogas and compost for urban farms.
ai_usage: AI optimizes waste collection routes and digester loading to maximize biogas production.
impact: 500 tons of compost produced per year
long_description:
Food waste is a major contributor to landfill methane emissions, and many urban farms struggle to access affordable compost. A network of community-scale anaerobic digesters offers a circular solution: organic waste from households and businesses is processed into biogas for heating or electricity and nutrient-rich compost for local agriculture. This reduces waste disposal costs, creates local green jobs, and strengthens urban food resilience.

AI optimizes collection routes and digester loading to maximize biogas yield and minimize operational costs. Success means 10,000 tons of waste diverted annually, 500 tons of compost produced, and a replicable model for other neighborhoods. By closing the loop between waste and food production, the network turns a liability into an asset, fostering community engagement and environmental stewardship.

title: Food Prescription Program
description: Health systems and clinics prescribe 'food prescriptions' to patients with diet-related conditions, redeemable for fresh produce at participating farmers markets and grocery stores.
ai_usage: AI matches patient dietary needs with available produce inventory and tracks redemption and health outcomes.
long_description:
Food prescriptions bridge the gap between clinical care and community food access. For patients with diet-related conditions like diabetes or hypertension, fresh produce is medicine. By partnering with clinics and farmers markets, this program turns a doctor's recommendation into a tangible, healthy resource. It addresses food insecurity as a health issue, not just a social one, and supports local farmers.

The program works by having healthcare providers screen patients for food insecurity and diet-related conditions, then prescribe a monthly dollar amount for fresh produce. Patients redeem these prescriptions at participating markets, where AI helps tailor choices to their dietary needs and tracks usage. Success means improved health outcomes, reduced emergency visits, and a sustainable funding model. With 3,000 patients and a 65% redemption rate, this initiative can become a national model for healthcare and food systems collaboration.

title: Neighborhood Food Hub
description: Community centers in targeted neighborhoods host food co-ops, cooking classes, and a community kitchen with subsidized rental spaces for local food entrepreneurs.
ai_usage: AI analyzes food sales and class attendance to tailor programming and inventory to community needs.
long_description: Food deserts in St. Louis leave thousands without access to fresh, affordable food, undermining health and community vitality. The Neighborhood Food Hub transforms underutilized community centers into vibrant food hubs, offering a co-op market, cooking classes, and a shared commercial kitchen. This model rebuilds local food systems from the ground up, empowering residents to take ownership of their food environment and fostering economic opportunity for aspiring food entrepreneurs. Success is measured by sustained community engagement, increased food access, and the launch of viable local food businesses that create jobs and reinvest in the neighborhood.

title: School Food Recovery Network
description: St. Louis Public Schools partner with food banks to redistribute uneaten cafeteria food to after-school programs and community fridges.
ai_usage: AI predicts cafeteria surplus volumes to streamline donation pickups and reduce waste.
impact: 15,000 lbs of food rescued per month
long_description: In St. Louis, thousands of children rely on school meals, yet tons of edible food are thrown away daily. This waste is both a moral and environmental failure. The School Food Recovery Network turns this problem into a solution by connecting schools with community fridges and after-school programs, ensuring surplus food feeds hungry families instead of landfills. AI-driven forecasting matches donations with demand, making the process efficient and reliable. Success means every partner school reduces waste, every community fridge stays stocked, and no child in our city goes to bed hungry. This initiative not only addresses food insecurity but also models a circular, community-centered approach to food systems.

title: Urban Food Forest Initiative
description: Convert vacant lots across St. Louis into food forests with fruit/nut trees and berry bushes, managed by neighborhood associations and local nonprofits.
ai_usage: AI identifies optimal vacant lot locations based on soil quality, sunlight, and proximity to food deserts.
long_description:
St. Louis has over 1,200 vacant lots, many in food deserts where residents lack access to fresh produce. Urban food forests transform these liabilities into community assets, providing free, perennial sources of fruit, nuts, and berries while improving soil health, air quality, and neighborhood cohesion. Managed by local nonprofits and neighborhood associations, these forests become self-sustaining ecosystems that require minimal maintenance once established.

Success looks like a network of 50 food forests across the city, each serving an average of 2,000 residents. Communities gain not only food but also green space, educational opportunities, and a sense of stewardship. The initiative reduces food insecurity, mitigates urban heat islands, and demonstrates how technology can drive equitable urban agriculture.
